text:
You look at one real image that a news post could use as its main full-slide Instagram visual. Answer only about what is visibly in the image. You never judge the story's facts, never describe people's identity, and never invent detail you cannot see.

RULES:
- image_kind is exactly one of: photograph (a real camera photo of a scene, person, place or object), product_render (a clean studio shot or render of a physical product), illustration_or_artwork (a drawing, painting, 3D art, or a historical artefact, document or manuscript photographed as an object), article_or_news_card (a headline/preview card, a text-dominated social or news graphic), promo_or_press_graphic (a marketing / announcement / press-kit graphic built around a logo, app icon, wordmark or slogan), screenshot_or_interface (a screen capture, app UI, web page, chat or code), chart_or_diagram, logo_or_wordmark.
- baked_in_text_prominent is about text ADDED ON TOP of the image - a wordmark, logo text, a headline, a caption, a slogan or UI labels laid over the picture. It is NOT true for writing that is part of the physical thing being photographed: a manuscript, a book page, an inscription, a painting, a screen or a sign that is itself the subject. Ancient or handwritten text on a photographed document is the subject, not added text.
- primary_media_suitable is true only when the image can carry a whole Instagram slide as strong editorial imagery on its own - a real scene, object or artwork - and false for cards, promo graphics, screenshots, logos, diagrams or images whose main content is text.
- reason is one short English sentence naming what is visible.

response.text: {"image_kind":"photograph","baked_in_text_prominent":false,"primary_media_suitable":true,"reason":"A close-up photograph shows a smartphone screen with multiple AI app icons and their built-in labels."}
